notes:
Identity assessment: supplied canonical text is a journal-article PDF text parse with title "Self-Control as Limited Resource: Regulatory Depletion Patterns", authors Mark Muraven, Dianne M. Tice, and Roy F. Baumeister, Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 1998, Vol. 74, No. 3, 774-789. These identify the referenced primary work; DOI is not visibly printed in the inspected header. Text includes article sections and references through p. 789. No PDF path was supplied, so visual/OCR confirmation was unavailable. Input study_o=2 conflicts with the emotional-control conditions and locator p. 5: those conditions are Study 1, printed pp. 777-778 (fifth page of the article at p. 778). Actual Study 2 uses thought suppression/expression and unsolvable-anagram persistence, pp. 779-780. Description supplies a condition but no outcome or test; p. 778 reports manipulation checks, between-condition handgrip contrasts, and within-condition pre/post handgrip tests. No target chosen from input order or numeric agreement. Candidate evidence for No emotional control: Within-condition handgrip change versus zero: canonical OCR "*(19) < 1, ns"; ns provides no numeric p bound. This condition is also the comparator in the decrease-versus-control (canonical f(38)=1.98, p<.05) and increase-versus-control (canonical f(38)=2.32, p<.025) handgrip contrasts. These f/* characters are retained as OCR candidates, not verified metric identities. Table 1 reports n = 20 in each condition for handgrip performance; this is a candidate condition-specific participant N, not an established N for the assigned test. No N inferred from df, and no group sum selected. Printed p bounds remain attached to their candidate tests. The Study 1 footnote says one increase-condition participant did not answer the effort question and was omitted only from analyses involving that question.
